summary: Reviewed 3 modified files: knowledge.js, api-client.js, styles.css. Performed full OWASP Top 10 assessment. 0 Critical, 0 High findings. 1 Medium (pre-existing, non-blocking, documented). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A03 XSS — PASS. All server-supplied string values interpolated into HTML use escapeHtml() guards throughout knowledge.js. origin_plan is doubly-encoded: encodeURIComponent() in the href attribute and escapeHtml() in the link text (lines 199–200). superseded_by is a numeric type from server JSON and is concatenated directly ('KN-' + ins.superseded_by, line 133) — safe. Inline error messages use escapeHtml(err.message || String(err)) (lines 502, 421, 435, 453). No raw innerHTML writes of unsanitised user input found.

A05 Security Misconfiguration / A01 Broken Access Control — MEDIUM (pre-existing, non-blocking). api-knowledge.ts handleDeleteKnowledge (line 303) and handlePromoteKnowledge (line 371): repository_name query parameter is NOT validated against PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX at the handler layer. The storage layer's _validateSlug() prevents path traversal before any file path is constructed, so no security breach is possible. However, a malformed slug causes _validateSlug() to throw a generic Error (not an ApiError), which propagates to the unhandled-error branch and returns HTTP 500 instead of a well-typed HTTP 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. This is a documented known limitation in the file's @known-limitation comment. Contrast: handleMoveKnowledge and handleUpdateKnowledge both validate repository_name via Zod PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX before storage access. Recommended fix: add an explicit z.string().regex(PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX) guard to handleDeleteKnowledge and handlePromoteKnowledge to return consistent 400 responses and eliminate reliance on the storage layer as the sole validation point. This was NOT introduced by WP-008 — it pre-dates this work package.

A01 Broken Access Control — INFO. This is an internal developer-tool SPA served on localhost. No authentication or session management layer is present — consistent with the tool's intended audience and deployment model. No access control regressions introduced by WP-008.

A03 Injection (API layer) — PASS. api-client.js buildQueryString() uses encodeURIComponent() on all key/value pairs (line 45), preventing query-string injection. URL path segments (id, slug) are encoded via encodeURIComponent() at all call sites. Request bodies are serialised via JSON.stringify(), preventing injection through body parameters. moveKnowledge() passes targetRepositoryName directly to the JSON body without coercion — this is validated server-side by KnowledgeMoveBodySchema z.string().regex(PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX), providing proper server-side input validation.

A04 Insecure Design — PASS. scopeBadgeClass (knowledge.js line 117) is derived from ins.scope but only two hardcoded CSS class name strings are emitted based on a boolean check (isGlobal ? ... : ...) — ins.scope is never interpolated directly into HTML. No direct data-to-HTML injection path through scope values.

A06 Vulnerable & Outdated Components — PASS. No new third-party dependencies introduced in knowledge.js, api-client.js, or styles.css. All changes are vanilla ES5/CSS with no external library additions.

summary: Code review PASS. Reviewed knowledge.js (518 lines), api-client.js (knowledge methods, lines 100–212), and styles.css (.badge-scope-repository rules). All 7 ACs confirmed met. Architecture is sound — correct use of closures for encapsulated view state, clean event delegation pattern, partial re-render strategy (renderFilterBar/renderList separation) correctly prevents focus-theft regression. No blocking issues found. One documentation-forward item tagged for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: No blocking issues found. Code is clean and consistent with the codebase's vanilla ES5 SPA patterns.

Partial re-render architecture (renderFilterBar + renderList as separate concerns) is the correct approach. renderFilterBar is only invoked on tab change (when the bar layout changes), and renderList is called for all other state mutations. This avoids the focus-theft regression that a full re-render on every keystroke would cause. The inline comment (lines 257–262) accurately documents the rationale.

Post-promote and post-move optimistic update pattern (filter from allInsights + push newInsight + renderList) is correct. The promoted insight gains scope='global', so it disappears from the repository tab filter correctly via applyFilters(). User must switch to Global tab to see the promoted insight — this is expected SPA behaviour and consistent with prior art in this codebase. Not a bug.

getDistinctValues() collects repository_name values from ALL insights (not just the currently filtered set). This is correct — the filter dropdown should offer all known repositories, not just those matching current filters, to avoid the 'vanishing options' problem where selecting a filter removes other options.

api-client.js knowledge methods are well-documented: each has a JSDoc with @param types, a description of the falsy-coercion behaviour (|| undefined), and explicit mention of the '0'-string edge-case as a known limitation. This is commendable documentation discipline for a vanilla JS codebase.

[documentation-forward] The Move action's target repository input uses placeholder='target-repository-name' (the literal field name). End-user documentation or a tooltip should clarify that this expects a repository slug (e.g. 'my-project', 'ai-insights'), not a display label. The README or in-app help should document valid repository name format (matching PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX on the server side).
